artifacts.synopsis: TE Huffman filed an appeal after the 50th GA amended BCO 38-1 to change the remedy from complaint to appeal, but his case originated and was nearly complete under the prior rule allowing complaint. The SJC found the case judicially out of order and remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery to adjudicate as a complaint under the then-existing rule, resetting the clock for presbytery action.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.

artifacts.title: Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
artifacts.synopsis: Bumgarner, a ruling elder who had been deposed in 2012, filed a BCO 40-5 application in 2015 seeking reversal of the censure after having previously withdrawn his complaint and acknowledged it could not be resubmitted. The SJC dismissed the application as administratively out of order because it sought to re-file a withdrawn complaint and because BCO 40-3 prohibits reversal of judicial censures except by appeal or complaint.

artifacts.synopsis: TE John Hardie appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Metro Atlanta Presbytery's judicial commission, raising seventeen specifications of error under six categories including procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of indulgence, prejudice, and disproportionate censure. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error in MAP's proceedings and upholding the indefinite suspension.

artifacts.title: Latimer v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Rev. Latimer's appeal from his deposition for allegedly pursuing an unbiblical divorce, finding that Presbytery clearly erred because the record contained no conclusive evidence that his divorce filing — made on advice of counsel to protect his children — reflected an intent to divorce rather than a defensive legal measure; two concurring opinions addressed the Presbytery's choice of definite versus indefinite suspension.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Charles Tarter appealed Evangel Presbytery's guilty verdict and censure after it convicted him of teaching a view of the creation days contrary to the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the appeal, vacated the judgment and censure, and remanded the matter because Presbytery had not followed the constitutional process for examining and recording a minister's stated differences; Presbytery was directed either to conduct that process or dismiss the case.

artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in finding no strong presumption of guilt in TE Joshua Moon after an investigation into allegations that his theological views on Federal Vision topics were heterodox, holding that deference to the presbytery was required absent clear error in the record. The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal by TE Paul W. Lee against Korean Southwest Presbytery's judgment finding him guilty of disobeying citations, rejecting admonitions, and other charges. The Standing Judicial Commission found KSWP erred on all issues through procedural violations including improper admonishment of judicial commission members mid-trial, failure to record trial proceedings, denial of cross-examination rights, and improper censure. Case remanded for retrial or dismissal.
